title: Software
text:
WimPyDD
A Python NREFT framework for dark matter–nucleus direct detection. Used in the LZ analysis and by the COSINE-100 collaboration.
Webpage · Documentation


WimPyC
An extension module of WimPyDD for dark matter capture in celestial bodies (Sun, Earth and others), for single-scattering capture.
Webpage · Documentation

title: Gaurav Tomar
text:
Research interests: Dark matter · Direct detection · NREFT · Celestial probes
I am one the lead developers of WimPyDD and WimPyC, open-source tools for dark matter direct detection and celestial-body capture, adopted by the LZ and COSINE-100 collaborations. Currently, I am a Principal Researcher at the Center for Quantum SpaceTime (CQUeST), Sogang University, Seoul.

title: Research
text:
My research centers on model-independent NREFT dark matter phenomenology, applied across three connected fronts.

Direct detection
Non-relativistic effective field theory allows the full space of DM-nucleus interaction operators, beyond simple spin-independent / spin-dependent scattering, to be confronted with experimental data. This work underlies WimPyDD, which is used in the LZ analysis and by the COSINE-100 collaboration.


Celestial-body capture
Dark matter captured by the Sun, Earth, or other bodies can annihilate and leave observable signals, from neutrinos to the heating of planets and stars. My work includes the code WimPyC for capture in celestial bodies, which I used to study dark matter with electromagnetic interactions. Neutrinos from the Sun and Earth, and the heating of Jupiter and white dwarfs, give the strongest limits in some parameter regions.


Sub-GeV dark matter
Light dark matter below standard nuclear-recoil thresholds can still be probed through the Migdal effect, a small, calculable probability of electron ionization accompanying a nuclear recoil. I compute Migdal rates for direct-detection and neutrino-experiment targets, including the liquid scintillator of JUNO. This work also provides an analytical expression for the ionization probability of hydrogen.

I am always open to new collaborations on these topics. Please get in touch via the Contact page.
